samples.summary: `seg()` is added as two byte-identical copies (packages/cli/src/client/url.ts and packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts) while `@wafflebase/core` already ships a `/url` subpath that exists precisely as the shared URL-safety primitive home (`isSafeUrl`/`SAFE_PROTOCOLS`, packages/core/src/url/index.ts, whose own header documents the 'previously duplicated across packages, hoisted here' pattern). docs/design/README.md line 166 lists `/url` as a shipped core subpath, and packages/frontend/package.json already depends on `@wafflebase/core`, so at minimum the frontend copy should have been `@wafflebase/core/url`. The change instead institutionalises the duplication in prose (docs/design/frontend.md: 'The CLI enforces the same rule ... with its own copy'), which is the reuse expectation this repo states it works against. The CLI's lack of a core dependency is a defensible reason for one copy, but it is not addressed as a tradeoff anywhere.

samples.summary: Scope: the change bundles four independent concerns behind one review — (a) one-segment id encoding across CLI + frontend, (b) a full rewrite of the CLI's upstream-error classification contract (forwardUpstreamError/upstreamErrorJson/UpstreamHttpError plus a documented exit-code contract change from '2 = system error' to '2 reserved'), (c) a new SSRF guard on the image fetcher with DNS resolution, manual redirect handling and a brand-new operator env var, and (d) a change to how `files download` picks its output filename. No originating issue accompanies the change to tie these together, and each is independently revertable/reviewable. Flagging as a scope observation, not a blocker.

samples.summary: The dot-segment rule now exists in three places with two different implementations: `seg()` (CLI), `seg()` (frontend), and `assertNoDotSegments()` in dry-run.ts, which re-derives the check with its own ad-hoc `split('?')[0].split('/')` query-string parser. The stated justification (a backstop for a future forgetful call site) is reasonable, but a shared `assertSegments(path)` exported from client/url.ts alongside `seg()` would keep one definition of the invariant instead of a second parser that can drift from the first.

samples.summary: Layering: ~200 lines of HTTP-response semantics (isErrorEnvelope, upstreamDetail, safeEnvelope, upstreamMessage, UpstreamHttpError, forwardUpstreamError, upstreamErrorJson) land in `output/formatter.ts`, whose stated job is rendering values in the selected `--format`. Deciding what a backend body means — envelope vs Nest default vs HTML page — is client-layer knowledge, and `HttpClient` already synthesizes one envelope itself (`sessionExpiredBody`). Two modules now own the envelope contract from opposite sides; `client/` (or a small `errors.ts`) would keep the classifier next to the transport that produces the bodies.

samples.summary: `seg(String(userId))` wraps a value typed `number` — it can never contain a separator or be a dot segment, so the call adds noise and slightly dilutes the signal that `seg()` marks an untrusted string id. Either drop it or note why uniformity was preferred.

The image fetcher (now carrying the whole URL/DNS/redirect guard) lives under `packages/cli/src/docs/`, but it is consumed by the slides PPTX export path too (packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:209). Pre-existing placement, but this change turns the file into a cross-namespace security primitive, which makes a neutral home (e.g. `src/client/` or `src/net/`) the better fit and would match how `seg()` was placed for the same reason.

verdict.reason: Every claimed fact verified in the tree. `seg()` exists twice with functionally identical bodies: packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts:18-23 and packages/cli/src/client/url.ts:24-29 (dot-segment throw + encodeURIComponent; only quote style differs). @wafflebase/core does ship a `/url` subpath explicitly documented as the home for hoisted URL-safety primitives (packages/core/src/url/index.ts:1-8 "Previously duplicated across the engine packages ... Hoisted here"; packages/core/package.json:25-30 exports "./url"), and docs/design/README.md:166 lists it as shipped. packages/frontend/package.json:57 already depends on @wafflebase/core, so the frontend copy could have been an import; the CLI has no core dep (packages/cli/package.json:36-37). The new design-doc prose records the duplication as intended (docs/design/frontend.md:465-467 "with its own copy"; docs/design/cli.md:1160-1163) without weighing it against the stated core-hoisting pattern. This is squarely in the design-fit lane (duplication/reuse, layer placement); no not-present, guard, or scope ground refutes it.

finding.summary: Frontend-wide URL rule + new `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts` primitive is documented only in the CLI design doc; the canonical frontend subsystem doc is untouched
finding.evidence: The change introduces a new shared frontend primitive (`packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts`) and applies it across every browser API module (documents, workspaces, folders, share-links, datasources, files, analytics, miro, spreadsheet image upload). The only design-doc record of this is a paragraph inside `docs/design/cli.md` §10 ("The rule is not CLI-only… `seg()`, `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts`… applied to **every** browser API module"). `docs/design/frontend.md` — the canonical doc for the browser client, which already documents the API layer and `fetchWithAuth` 401 handling at lines ~412-445 — contains no mention of `seg`, `url.ts`, or the path-segment rule (grep for `seg\(|url.ts|path segment` in docs/design/frontend.md: no matches). CONTRIBUTING/design discipline expects an architecture rule to be folded into the canonical subsystem doc rather than described from a neighbouring package's doc; as written, a future frontend contributor reading frontend.md has no way to learn that every route-param id must go through `seg()`. Also note the top-level backtick-path check does not validate that cli.md's frontend claims stay true as frontend modules are added.

verdict.reason: The canonical frontend subsystem doc is NOT untouched. docs/design/frontend.md:438-467 has a dedicated subsection "Request URLs: one id, one segment" that names `seg()`, cites the primitive's location `packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts`, declares it a rule for the whole API layer (listing document, workspace, folder, share link, datasource, file, analytics), shows a usage example, explains the `.`/`..` refusal, instructs contributors to apply `seg()` at every new interpolation, and cross-links the CLI copy plus docs/design/cli.md §10 for the end-to-end argument. The reviewer's claimed grep result ("no matches for seg\(|url.ts|path segment in frontend.md") is false against this tree: the same grep hits frontend.md lines 441, 442, 446. The referenced primitive packages/frontend/src/api/url.ts exists (alongside url.test.ts), so the doc reference is accurate rather than stale. The design-doc-discipline concern — that the rule lives only in a neighbouring package's doc and a frontend contributor could not learn it from frontend.md — is directly contradicted.
